title: OpenAI Foundation commits more than $125 million to public health datasets
friendlyTitle: More than $125 million will support open health research data
summary: The OpenAI Foundation announced an initial group of grants worth more than $125 million to create and preserve broadly available life-science data. Projects include drug-absorption benchmarks, records from failed drug programs and multimodal data for personalised cancer-vaccine research.
friendlySummary: The OpenAI Foundation is funding datasets about medicines, failed drug programs and personalised cancer vaccines. It says the data should be widely available to researchers.
whyItMatters: Better models cannot recover measurements that were never collected or records that have disappeared. If the funded datasets are released with meaningful privacy, consent and documentation, researchers beyond large laboratories could test ideas against evidence that is currently scarce or fragmented.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Good AI research needs good evidence. Open data can help more researchers work on health problems, but patient privacy and consent must remain strong.
